description: Initial lazy-root benchmark harness compile failed because Nickel Context::eval_shallow() returns NickelError directly; added plan to map NickelError into local benchmark Error before rerunning.

Initial lazy-root autoresearch harness: added wide checked-in fixture, shallow discovery benchmark, eager selected-root baseline, and checks. Baseline medians show selected_root_total_wall_ns=72.4ms with current eager path forcing all 128 roots.

Selected-root force now uses a wrapper evaluation of only the requested record field instead of eager all-root extraction. Benchmark counts drop from 128/127 to 1/0 and selected_root_total_wall_ns improves from 72.4ms to 64.3ms while all_roots_total_wall_ns guardrail stays 38.9ms.

Reused one Nickel Context across discovery and selected-root force by importing the fixture through a synthetic session source. Selected_root_force_wall_ns dropped from 32.2ms to 0.27ms while discovery stayed ~32.7ms; selected_root_total_wall_ns improved from 64.3ms to 33.0ms with counts still 1/0.

Confirmation rerun of the shared-Context wrapper benchmark. Same code reproduced the big win: selected_root_total_wall_ns nudged from 32.98ms to 32.87ms, keeping discovery ~32.5ms and selected_root_force_wall_ns under 0.30ms.

Tried nickel-lang-core Program-backed discovery and selected-root forcing. Big regression: selected_root_total_wall_ns jumped to 127.7ms and discovery alone to 126.7ms, so Program::query/eval_full_for_export is much heavier than the current Context+wrapper path for this workload.

Tried refining the nickel-lang-core path to use Program::parse() for syntactic top-level record labels plus Program field selection for selected-root force. It crashed before benchmarking: Program::parse() panicked inside nickel-lang-core with `File parsed and then immediately accessed doesn't exist`, so this path is not stable enough for the loop.

Tried replacing eval_shallow-based discovery with wrapper `std.record.fields(import fixture)` via eval_deep_for_export, while moving benchmark/check scripts to a disk-backed CARGO_TARGET_DIR. Discovery regressed badly: root_discovery_wall_ns rose from ~32.5ms to 42.6ms and selected_root_total_wall_ns to 43.1ms, so deep export of field names defeats the shared-Context win even though force still stayed under 0.5ms.

Tried discovering root labels from the already-read fixture source string with Context::eval_shallow(source) while still forcing the selected root via the import-wrapper path. Mixed result: discovery improved to 31.6ms, but selected_root_force_wall_ns regressed to 3.47ms, so losing the old import-cache reuse made selected_root_total_wall_ns land at 35.2ms instead of the 32.9ms best.

Tried keeping the shallow root record alive and forcing only the selected field with Context::eval_expr_shallow before direct to_serde deserialization. Nickel only reduced the field to WHNF: CrunchDerivation deserialization failed with `invalid type: Other, expected: String`, so at least one derivation field still needs recursive forcing beyond a single shallow step.

Prototype public-API fast path: reuse one shallow root record, then lazily force only the selected derivation and manually decode simple string/array fields. It improved selected_root_total_wall_ns to 32.31ms with selected_root_force_wall_ns down to 0.20ms, but the implementation only handled the benchmark fixture shape (no env/inputs/fixed_output/provenance) inside example support, so it is not general enough to keep yet.

Generalized the fast path into production seams: `crunch_eval::ShallowRecordSession` now keeps one shallow top-level record alive, and `crunch_glue::decode_crunch_derivation_lazy()` recursively forces only the selected derivation fields. Benchmark improved from 32.87ms to 32.32ms total with selected_root_force_wall_ns down to 0.19ms, while new tests cover bad siblings plus nested env/inputs/fixed_output/provenance so the win is not fixture-only.

Added `ShallowRecordSession::scan_for_label()` so selected-root discovery can scan the shallow top-level record for count+target presence without allocating owned label strings on the hot path. Benchmark improved from 32.32ms to 31.97ms total while preserving root_count=128, selected-label validation, and the same lazy selected-root force path.

Made `ShallowRecordSession::scan_for_label()` use the shallow record’s O(1)-style metadata path (`len()` plus direct field lookup) instead of iterating every top-level field. That keeps the selected-root discovery API general while dropping selected_root_total_wall_ns from 31.97ms to 31.25ms and root_discovery_wall_ns to 31.06ms on the same 128-root fixture.

Tried fusing discovery and selection into one `scan_and_select_field()` helper so benchmark path could reuse the selected Expr instead of looking it up twice. First compile failed because the new `SelectedTopLevelField` derived `Debug`, but `nickel_lang::Expr` is not `Debug`; fix is trivial, then rerun to measure whether the saved lookup matters.

Tried fusing discovery and selection into one `scan_and_select_field()` helper so the benchmark could reuse the selected Expr and skip a second lookup. Big regression: cloning the selected field Expr during discovery was much more expensive than the cheap presence probe, pushing selected_root_total_wall_ns to 53.9ms and root_discovery_wall_ns to 53.4ms.

Added `ShallowRecordSession::field_count()` and stopped re-checking selected-label presence during discovery. The selected-root path now counts top-level roots in discovery and lets the force step own selected-field lookup, which dropped selected_root_total_wall_ns from 31.25ms to 30.42ms and root_discovery_wall_ns to 30.24ms without changing force counts or the 128-root guardrail.

Tried pre-scanning derivation records into a `DerivationFieldExprs` struct so lazy decode could trade repeated named lookups for one iterator pass. It regressed badly: selected_root_total_wall_ns rose to 32.38ms and selected_root_force_wall_ns to 0.23ms, so the extra top-level iteration and field collection cost more than the old direct lookups on this workload.

Tried caching `nickel_lang::Record` handles through lazy derivation decode so the hot path would avoid repeated `Expr::as_record()` calls and named-lookups would share one borrowed record view. It regressed to 32.98ms total and 0.22ms selected-force, so the extra wrapper plumbing and record-handle threading cost more than the old direct helper calls.

Tried precomputing a reusable `ShallowRecordSessionConfig` so repeated benchmark samples could skip re-deriving source-name and import-path metadata before each `eval_shallow`. It regressed to 32.69ms total and 32.48ms discovery, so cloning the prepared config each sample was slower than rebuilding those tiny path-derived values inline.

Tried caching top-level field count inside `ShallowRecordSession` so discovery would avoid a second `as_record().len()` after `eval_shallow`. It regressed badly to 43.34ms total and 43.05ms discovery; whatever borrow/layout/codegen change that added around session construction outweighed the saved lookup, so keep field_count computed on demand.

Tried making `ShallowRecordSession::field_count()` and `scan_for_label()` infallible now that the session constructor already validates top-level roots. That should have been a pure API/codegen cleanup, but benchmark cratered to 122.3ms total and 121.4ms discovery, so this reshaping clearly hurt optimized codegen on the hot path and is not worth keeping.

Tried a general simple-derivation fast path in `decode_crunch_derivation_lazy()` that detects absent complex fields (`env`/`inputs`/`fixed_output`/`provenance`) and decodes simple roots through direct `Record` lookups before falling back. It cratered to 73.10ms total and 72.44ms discovery, so the extra branch/helper layer hurt codegen far more than it saved on the benchmark’s simple derivations.

Tried adding `#[inline]` hints on hot `ShallowRecordSession` and lazy-derivation decode helpers to encourage cross-crate inlining across the benchmark path. It still regressed from 30.42ms to 31.18ms total, so the compiler’s default inlining choices were better than the forced hints here.

Baseline re-measurement at session start. Current best code from prior session (field_count + no redundant label check). selected_root_total=32.97ms, discovery=32.77ms, force=0.20ms. Prior session best was 30.42ms median — variance is expected across sessions.

asi.bottleneck: discovery is 99.4% of total — almost entirely Nickel eval_shallow cost
asi.force_status: 0.20ms is negligible, no room to optimize
asi.nickel_api: eval_shallow is the cheapest Nickel API (WHNF only), can't go lower
asi.prior_dead_ends: inline hints, caching field_count, precomputing config, fusing scan+select, DerivationFieldExprs pre-scan, Record handle caching — all regressed
asi.remaining_angles: Context::new() overhead isolation, import_paths Vec allocation, source_name String allocation, reduce fixture-independent per-session overhead, profile parsing vs VM eval split

description: Implemented isolated-worker bounded root forcing, streamed pipeline eval/convert into the worker, added parallel all-root benchmark coverage and captured the first parallel_all_roots_total_wall_ns baseline bundle for the wide fixture.

Tried reducing parallel all-root overhead by reusing one isolated session per worker chunk instead of reopening a session per label. Benchmark run crashed before measurement because Cargo target dir `target/autoresearch-parallel-root` became unusable (`quote` failed with `E0463: can't find crate proc_macro2`) after prior test/build reuse.

Reduced bounded parallel all-root overhead by reusing one isolated EvaluationSession per worker chunk instead of reopening a worker session per label. Also switched autoresearch to fresh per-run Cargo target dirs to avoid shared-target corruption and benchmark contamination.

Reused coordinator-discovered root shape and labels inside IsolatedWorkerInput so worker sessions skip repeated shallow discovery before deep forcing. This trims bounded parallel all-root time slightly beyond the per-worker-session reuse change.

Tried pre-resolving requested labels to top-level indexes and skipping per-force label lookup inside worker sessions. That extra assignment/index plumbing regressed parallel_all_roots_total_wall_ns badly (281.6ms vs 113.4ms), so revert and keep the simpler worker-chunk session reuse design.

Applied the coordinator-derived worker metadata to the actual bounded parallel path: force_worker_assignment now opens worker sessions from cached shape+labels via open_worker_source instead of re-running shallow discovery in each worker. This removes redundant per-worker discovery before deep forcing.

Shrank worker-session label metadata to each worker chunk's requested subset instead of cloning the full discovered root-label list into every worker session. This keeps the cached shape reuse but trims per-worker label cloning and lookup work.

Tried reducing worker-input clone cost by converting session/worker source metadata to Arc-backed shared state (`Arc<str>`, `Arc<[OsString]>`, `Arc<[RootLabel]>`). The benchmark command crashed before measurement with a transient Cargo build failure (`can't find crate for gix_odb` / `fuse_backend_rs`) while compiling vendor dependencies into a fresh target dir.

Hypothesis: Arc-back shared IsolatedWorkerInput metadata (source/import_paths/source_name/labels) would cut worker-input clone cost across bounded parallel all-roots. Result: compile-path transient gone, but benchmark still regressed to 109.5ms vs 108.3ms best, so clone savings do not beat Arc conversion/to_vec overhead on worker-session open. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: leave worker metadata owned/simple and look at chunk scheduling or per-root deep-force costs instead.

Hypothesis: avoid full per-worker deep export by deep-evaluating only the selected top-level field through a new `Context::eval_expr_deep_for_export` helper in Nickel, reusing one worker shallow top-level expr. Crash: crunch-eval depends on crates.io `nickel-lang` 2.0.0 here, not the edited vendored source, so the new helper was invisible at compile time; worker error plumbing also tried `to_string()` on raw `nickel_lang::Error`. Rollback reason: experiment could not compile. Next action hint: use only existing public Nickel APIs in crunch-eval, or patch dependency source first before trying new Context methods.

Hypothesis: add adaptive serial fallback for bounded selected/all-root forcing when each worker chunk would be tiny, so small jobs avoid thread/session overhead and reuse one deep-export session. Crash: first cut mismatched the current Arc-backed `open_worker_source` signature and failed to compile with `expected Arc<[OsString]>` / `expected Arc<str>`. Rollback reason: compile error in fallback helper. Next action hint: keep the fallback idea but match the live worker-input types, then rerun.

Hypothesis: bounded root forcing should fall back to one serial worker session when each worker chunk is tiny (chunk_len <= 4), avoiding thread/session overhead on small jobs like the 16-root wide fixture at concurrency=4. Result regressed badly to 117.6ms vs 108.3ms best, so the serial fallback lost more than it saved under the current Arc-backed worker-input path. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep bounded parallel dispatch for this workload and inspect why the serial helper path is slower than the existing eager-all-roots guardrail before trying more routing heuristics.

Hypothesis: retest the tiny-chunk serial fallback on the real owned String/Vec worker metadata instead of the discarded Arc-backed variant, so small bounded jobs reuse one session without the Arc regression. Crash: first rebase back to owned worker metadata still left one `force_worker_assignment` call site passing owned clones into the restored `&[OsString]` / `&str` `open_worker_source` signature. Rollback reason: compile error from incomplete type rollback. Next action hint: finish the owned-worker rollback consistently, then rerun the serial-fallback measurement.

Switched bounded worker fan-out from `std::thread::spawn` to `std::thread::scope`, letting worker closures borrow the shared worker input instead of cloning it into `'static` threads. This dropped parallel_all_roots_total_wall_ns from the prior 108.3ms best to 106.6ms on the 16-root fixture; eager all-roots guardrail stayed healthy at 61.6ms and selected-root force counts remained 1/0.

Hypothesis: after switching to scoped threads, worker results already arrive in request order, so removing per-chunk label Vec clones and the final result sort should trim bounded fan-out overhead. Result cratered to 126.0ms vs 106.6ms best; the borrowed-slice/lifetime reshaping clearly hurt codegen more than it saved in tiny result handling. Rollback reason: much worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the simpler owned WorkerAssignment/result structs and look elsewhere, likely around session open or thread launch itself rather than final ordering bookkeeping.

Capped effective worker count so bounded forcing keeps at least 8 requested roots per worker before fanning out, which trims redundant whole-session worker setup on small root sets while still honoring the caller's upper concurrency bound. On the 16-root fixture this reduces effective workers from 4 to 2 and improves parallel_all_roots_total_wall_ns from 106.64ms to 106.21ms; selected-root counts stayed 1/0 and eager all-roots guardrail stayed healthy at 62.9ms.

Hypothesis: once effective worker count is clamped, worker hot path can skip a second string lookup by forcing roots from already-selected `RootLabel`s instead of calling `session.force_root(label)` and re-searching `session.labels`. Crash: first cut moved `worker_labels` into `open_worker_source` and then tried to iterate it again, so borrow checker rejected the worker loop. Rollback reason: compile error from ownership mistake in the known-label path. Next action hint: either iterate over `session.root_labels()` after session construction or clone only the small selected label vector before moving it.

Hypothesis: keep the known-RootLabel fast path but iterate the worker session’s own selected labels, so worker hot path avoids repeated string lookup without extra plumbing. Crash: borrowing `session.root_labels()` for iteration conflicts with the mutable borrow needed for `force_root_with_known_label`, so the compiler rejected the loop. Rollback reason: mutable/immutable borrow conflict in the worker loop. Next action hint: clone the small selected label vector once after session construction, then reuse those owned `RootLabel`s for the known-label force path.

Hypothesis: after worker-count clamping, preselected worker labels should drive forcing directly through a `force_root_with_known_label` helper, avoiding repeated `session.force_root(label)` linear scans over the small selected label set. Result cratered to 126.3ms vs 106.2ms best; cloning the selected labels once and reshaping the helper path hurt codegen far more than the tiny lookup cost. Rollback reason: much worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the plain string-label worker loop and focus on bigger overheads than per-root label lookup.

Hypothesis: raise `MIN_ROOTS_PER_WORKER` from 8 to 16 so the 16-root workload collapses to one worker, cutting one more whole-session deep-eval and thread launch from the bounded path. Result regressed slightly to 106.97ms vs 106.21ms best, so one-worker routing is a bit worse than the current two-worker clamp on this fixture. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the 8-roots-per-worker clamp and probe other worker-setup overheads instead of pushing all the way to one worker.

Hypothesis: tune the minimum-roots-per-worker clamp from 8 down to 6 so the 16-root workload uses 3 workers instead of 2, which might better balance redundant worker setup against available parallelism. Result regressed to 111.16ms vs 106.21ms best, so 3 workers are clearly worse than the current 2-worker clamp on this fixture. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the 8-root threshold; the local search now shows 1 worker slower, 3 workers slower, and 2 workers best so far.

Hypothesis: after switching to scoped threads, the old Arc-backed worker/session metadata may no longer help and owned String/Vec fields could give better codegen than Arc conversions. Result regressed to 108.02ms vs 106.21ms best, so the current Arc-backed metadata is still slightly better in the scoped+clamped path on this fixture. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the Arc-backed session metadata and probe other overheads instead of reverting that earlier reshape.

Hypothesis: specialize `force_all_roots_bounded` so the primary workload sends contiguous `RootLabel` chunks directly to workers instead of cloning a full `Vec<String>` and re-selecting labels by string before every worker session. Result exploded to 316.5ms vs 106.2ms best, so the dedicated all-roots worker path hurt codegen or duplicated enough setup to swamp the saved string-selection work. Rollback reason: catastrophically worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the shared selected-root worker machinery even for all-roots; the extra specialization is not worth it on this path.

Hypothesis: scoped workers already join in assignment order, so the final sort over `IndexedRoot.index` should be redundant and removable. Result regressed slightly to 106.83ms vs 106.21ms best, and the change also left an `IndexedRoot.index` warning behind, so the explicit sort is not worth touching here. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the current sort-and-index bookkeeping and search for a larger win than this tiny tail cleanup.

Hypothesis: session open still re-runs a full top-level `eval_shallow` during discovery, so deriving labels directly from the already-available `shallow_expr` from `open_source` should cut discovery overhead for the parallel benchmark. Result regressed badly to 152.78ms vs 106.21ms best, so this refactor hurt optimized codegen or invalidated a beneficial sharing path instead of saving work. Rollback reason: much worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the existing discovery flow; the duplicate-looking top-level shallow evaluation is apparently cheaper than this reshaped label-discovery helper path.

Hypothesis: with the current 2-worker clamp, one assignment can run on the caller thread while only the remaining assignments spawn helper threads, saving one spawn/join pair on the hot path. Result cratered to 273.39ms vs 106.21ms best, so this mixed local+spawn scheduling reshaped the hot path badly enough to swamp the saved spawn cost. Rollback reason: catastrophically worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the simpler all-scoped-worker fan-out; thread-count savings need a different design than this local-worker split.

Hypothesis: collect syscall-level evidence for the current best code by stracing the benchmark binary directly before more code changes. Crash: autoresearch harness rejected the command because this repo requires experiments to run through `./autoresearch.sh`, not custom benchmark invocations. Rollback reason: harness policy rejection, no code change measured. Next action hint: if more profiling evidence is needed, wrap the profiling tool around `./autoresearch.sh` itself or use non-experiment shell commands outside the autoresearch runner.

Hypothesis: worker threads are tiny and short-lived, so spawning them with a much smaller stack via `Builder::spawn_scoped(...).stack_size(512 KiB)` might trim spawn overhead and memory pressure. Result cratered to 233.63ms vs 106.21ms best, so custom builder-based spawning is far worse here than plain scoped-thread spawning. Rollback reason: catastrophically worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep default scoped-thread spawning; the builder path adds too much overhead on this hot path.

Hypothesis: for record-shaped root sets, each worker can wrap the original source into a smaller record containing only its assigned labels, so `eval_deep_for_export` forces only that subset instead of all roots in every worker session. Result cratered to 247.32ms vs 106.21ms best; the wrapper-source generation and Nickel field-projection path are far worse than the current full-source worker sessions on this fixture. Rollback reason: catastrophically worse primary metric. Next action hint: drop the wrapper-source idea from the hot path unless Nickel exposes a real per-expression deep-export API.

Hypothesis: patch crunch to use the vendored `nickel-lang`, add `Context::eval_expr_deep_for_export`, and change worker forcing to deep-export only each selected top-level field from one shallow worker expr instead of `eval_deep_for_export(full_source)` per worker. Result cratered to 267.89ms vs 106.21ms best, so this per-field deep-export path is much slower than the existing whole-session deep-export worker path on the wide fixture even when the API is available. Rollback reason: catastrophically worse primary metric. Next action hint: drop this path for now; remaining wins likely need thread reuse or different Nickel internals, not per-field export through the current public wrapper.

Hypothesis: once bounded forcing clamps to only 2 effective workers on the 16-root fixture, `force_all_roots_bounded` should bypass the isolated-worker path entirely and reuse the coordinator session’s eager `force_all_roots()` fast path, eliminating duplicate worker deep exports. Result still regressed badly to 138.34ms vs 106.21ms best, so this adaptive serial handoff does not inherit the standalone eager-all-roots guardrail cost the way expected. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep bounded all-roots on the current isolated-worker machinery; the eager serial path is not a drop-in win inside this API boundary.

Hypothesis: replace per-call scoped thread spawning with cached Rayon thread pools keyed by effective bounded concurrency, so repeated benchmark samples reuse worker threads instead of paying OS-thread spawn/join each call. Result cratered to 244.36ms vs 106.21ms best, so this Rayon pool path adds far more scheduling/abstraction overhead than it saves on the current worker workload. Rollback reason: catastrophically worse primary metric. Next action hint: drop external pool abstraction here; if thread reuse matters, it likely needs a much thinner purpose-built path.

Hypothesis: for the common 2-worker-clamped all-roots case, do one coordinator deep export and deserialize each extracted root through JSON instead of paying one whole-program deep export per worker. Crash: first cut borrowed `self` through `ensure_deep_expr()` while also mutating `forced_root_count`, so the compiler rejected the helper with E0503/E0506. Rollback reason: borrow-check failure in the coordinator JSON path. Next action hint: clone or otherwise detach the deep expr before the per-root loop, then rerun the single-deep-export experiment.

Hypothesis: for the common 2-worker-clamped all-roots case, do one coordinator deep export and deserialize each extracted root through JSON instead of paying one whole-program deep export per worker. Result still regressed badly to 153.58ms vs 106.21ms best, so the extra JSON export/parse path costs more than the duplicated worker deep exports it removes on this fixture. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: drop coordinator JSON deserialization as an optimization path; any single-deep-export design likely needs a much cheaper intermediate than JSON.

Hypothesis: replace per-call scoped thread spawning with a very thin custom persistent worker pool built from std channels and long-lived threads, avoiding the heavy Rayon abstraction that regressed earlier. Crash: first cut hit `E0310` because job results crossing the persistent pool threads need `T: 'static` on the pool submission path. Rollback reason: compile error from missing lifetime bound in the custom pool helper. Next action hint: add the explicit `'static` bound where the job result crosses the worker-thread boundary, then rerun the thin custom-pool experiment.
